model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log probability evaluated across various language models for different medical datasets. The horizontal axis contains the categories, labeled "Per-specialty terms," which are arranged alphabetically: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The vertical axis represents the value, labeled "Negative log probability," utilizing a linear scale that ranges from -22 at the top down to -27 at the bottom, with numeric tick mark intervals of 1. Because the scale descends numerically from top to bottom, all bars originate at the -22 baseline and extend downward. The chart features grouped bars, with each specialty category on the x-axis containing a cluster of seven individual bars. A legend at the top indicates that the first bar in every group, colored light blue, represents the "Mistralv0.2-Base" model. The subsequent six bars in each cluster denote models "Fine-tuned on:" specific specialties, rendered in a consistent color gradient: light beige for Cardio, light orange for Gastro, sandy orange for Infect, solid orange for Neuro, burnt orange for Obstetrics, and dark brown for Pediatrics. Visually, the light blue base model consistently forms the longest downward-extending bar in every category, reaching its lowest point of approximately -26.8 in the Cardio group, while its shortest length is approximately -23.8 in the Infect group. The six fine-tuned model bars in each group are consistently shorter, ending closer to the -22 baseline. The shortest bars overall are clustered in the Infect category, where the fine-tuned models range from approximately -23.0 to -23.2, while the deepest fine-tuned bars appear in the Cardio category, falling between roughly -25.8 and -26.1. The bars within each group maintain a strict order as dictated by the legend, and no specific bars are highlighted or annotated beyond the initial color coding.
